board.name: District of Columbia Board of Medicine (DC Health)

licence.title: Physician Assistant (PA) licence
licence.renewalDeadline: Last day of the birth month, in even or odd years matching the birth year (birth month cycle from June 16, 2024); legacy DCMR default December 31 of even years; the 2026 Board of Medicine notice cites June 30, 2026 for the current cohort
licence.transitionNote: DC Health moved all credentials to a birth month cycle: credentials issued or renewed from June 16, 2024 (renewals from September 2024) expire on the last day of the birth month; people born in even years get even expiration years and odd years get odd. During the one time transition, a licensee whose term was under 2 years owes 50% of the CE hours but still all of the 2 LGBTQ hours and the 10% public health hours. Ask the member for the expiration date printed on the licence.

ce.categoryRules: 40 hours Category 1 plus 60 hours Category 1 or 2 per 2 years; 2 hours LGBTQ cultural competency (Category 1 or equivalent, counts toward the 60); at least 10% (10 hours) in DC Director's public health priority topics
ce.nccpaNote: Current NCCPA PA-C certification substitutes for the 100 hours, but the 2 LGBTQ hours and the 10% public health priority hours are still required.
ce.firstRenewalExempt: only for a licence granted by examination (not reciprocity/endorsement)

topicMandates.topic: LGBTQ cultural competency or clinical treatment
topicMandates.appliesTo: all PAs, including those using NCCPA in lieu

topicMandates.topic: DC public health priorities (notice effective Oct 1, 2025): sexual and reproductive health; chronic disease management; One Health; healthcare professional retention and capacity building (suicide prevention, burnout, quality improvement, substance use disorder, implicit bias and cultural humility); community and patient safety (falls, violence prevention, emergency preparedness, social media, infection control, cognitive impairment)
topicMandates.appliesTo: all PAs (10% of required total), including those using NCCPA in lieu

ce.hivNote: D.C. Code 3-1205.10(b)(4) requires 3 HIV/AIDS credits for PAs, RNs and physicians unless waived by rule; 17 DCMR 4906.4(e) waives it for PAs and 5406.2 waives it for RNs.

practice.agreementTypeNote: Regulations use supervision with a delegation agreement; the statute (D.C. Code § 3-1201.02) defines PA practice as 'in collaboration with a licensed physician'.
practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: Written delegation agreement on the Board's form, signed by supervising physician(s) and PA, filed with the Board before practice begins and kept at the primary practice site; a new signed form is filed on any change; changes to supervising physicians filed within 10 days; termination form filed within 10 days; quarterly practice advisory review documented on file.
practice.notes: A physician may actively supervise no more than 4 on-duty PAs at one time. In outpatient settings supervision requires constant availability by electronic communication.

prescribing.csRegistrationNote: DC Controlled Substance Registration (biennial) through DC Health Pharmaceutical Control; the PA application must include the delegation agreement signed by supervising physician(s) who themselves hold a DC CSR. DEA separately. PDMP registration required for prescribers at renewal.

board.name: District of Columbia Board of Nursing (DC Health)

rn.renewalDeadline: June 30 of even years under DCMR (2026 renewal window April 1 to June 30, 2026), moving to the last day of the birth month under DC Health's transition
rn.nlcNote: DC is not a Nurse Licensure Compact jurisdiction; B26-0069 (NLC authorization) was pending in committee per secondary sources.

topicMandates.topic: LGBTQ cultural competency or specialized clinical training

topicMandates.appliesTo: all RNs (10% of 24; DC Health 2026 notice states 2.5)

rn.transitionNote: DC Health moved all credentials to a birth month cycle: credentials issued or renewed from June 16, 2024 (renewals from September 2024) expire on the last day of the birth month; people born in even years get even expiration years and odd years get odd. During the one time transition, a licensee whose term was under 2 years owes 50% of the CE hours but still all of the 2 LGBTQ hours and the 10% public health hours. Ask the member for the expiration date printed on the licence.

aprn.title: APRN; DCMR chapter 59 calls it a certificate to practice as a nurse-practitioner
aprn.separateLicenceOrCertificate: separate APRN credential (certificate under 17 DCMR ch. 59); requires current DC RN licence
aprn.renewalDeadline: Renews with the RN cycle (2026 notice: expires June 30, 2026), moving to birth month
aprn.pharmacologyNote: Adopted rule 17 DCMR 5903.5(c): 15 contact hours in the 2 years before the application date, specialty related, approved by ANCC or another Board recognized certifier, that "shall include a pharmacology component". DC Health's 2026 RN/APRN notice states "Fifteen (15) hours in pharmacology". The regulation sets no minimum pharmacology split; the Board's own notice treats all 15 as pharmacology. Show both, with the notice as the Board's current instruction.

upcoming.source: DC Health Second Notice of Proposed Rulemaking, 17 DCMR Ch. 57 to 60 (APRNs), D.C. Register Vol 73/23, June 5, 2026 (first proposed 71 DCR 010935, Sept 20, 2024)
upcoming.summary: Would retitle to certified nurse practitioner (CNP) licence; replace the 15 hour rule with 24 hours of CE per 2 years including 2 LGBTQ+ hours and 10% public health priority hours (first renewal exempt); let current national certification satisfy the hours except the LGBTQ+ and public health hours; waive the HIV mandate; add a controlled substances for pain section.

aprn.nationalCertNote: 17 DCMR 5903.5(b) names ANCC "or other national certifying body approved by the Board"; AANPCB is not named in the rule.

prescribing.pharmacologyCeForPrescribers: 15 contact hours per renewal with a pharmacology component (DC Health notice: 15 hours in pharmacology)
prescribing.csNote: DEA plus DC Controlled Substance Registration required before prescribing controlled substances; PDMP registration required for licence renewal of prescribers.

practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: None. The statutory collaboration section (D.C. Code § 3-1206.03) is repealed; APRNs act under general authorization in § 3-1206.01.
practice.note: D.C. Code 3-1206.02 (protocols) and 3-1206.03 (collaboration) are both repealed (D.C. Law 25-191, 2024); 17 DCMR 5910.1 still refers to "the protocol under which the nurse-practitioner is practicing", which is stale text.

unverified: DC controlled substance registration term and fee come from a DC Health Pharmaceutical Control letter marked REV 2/11 (biennial, $130); no current CSR rule or page stating the term was loaded.

Whether DC APRNs owe the 2 LGBTQ hours and 10% public health hours separately on the APRN credential under current rules: 17 DCMR ch. 59 (2004 text) is silent; they are met on the RN licence. The pending June 5, 2026 proposal would make them explicit for CNPs.
DC Nurse Licensure Compact status rests on the NCSBN map (secondary); no DC primary source was loaded.
Exact renewal date per licensee during the birth month transition: the app should take the expiration date printed on the licence.

DC PA supervision vs collaboration: statute (3-1201.02(13)) says collaboration; 17 DCMR 4914 to 4916 (last amended 2020) still require supervision, a filed delegation agreement and quarterly reviews. DCRegs shows no pending PA rulemaking.

No controlled substance specific CE requirement for DC PAs or APRNs exists in the adopted rules loaded; the pending APRN proposal adds CS for pain prescribing standards but not a CE hour mandate in the text reviewed.
sourceNote: dcregs.dc.gov section text was loaded by the chapter RuleList page postback, which downloads the adopted rule as a Word file (e.g. 174906.doc, 175903.doc).
corrections: DC PA: corrected the quote for D.C. Code 3-1201.02(13) to the exact loaded text.
DC PA: narrowed the first renewal exemption. 17 DCMR 4906.2 exempts only the first renewal of a licence granted by examination, not one granted by reciprocity.
DC PA and RN: confirmed in the loaded rules that the statutory 3 credit HIV/AIDS mandate is waived for both (4906.4(e), 5406.2) and added the RN fact.

DC both: added the birth year parity rule (even birth year, even expiry year) and the one time 50% CE proration for transition terms under 2 years, with LGBTQ and public health hours still due in full.
DC APRN: added the PDMP registration renewal condition with its primary quote (was only described in a note).

DC APRN: corrected the quote for the 2026 notice and removed the researcher's own "conservative reading" wording; the file now states the regulation text and the Board notice text side by side without inventing a split.

DC APRN: found a pending Second Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (June 5, 2026) that would replace the 15 hour pharmacology rule with 24 hours incl. LGBTQ+ and public health, accept national certification in lieu, and add CS for pain rules. Recorded as upcoming, not in effect.
DC APRN: added that the protocol statute (3-1206.02) is repealed along with collaboration (3-1206.03); 17 DCMR 5910.1 still mentions a protocol (stale).
DC RN: NLC non-membership now rests on the loaded NCSBN map (DC absent from the 43 enacted jurisdictions) instead of an unloaded LegiScan summary; still secondary, so verified:false.

DC both: expanded the public health priority domain list from the loaded 2025 notice; implicit bias, suicide prevention, SUD and infection control are qualifying examples within the 10%, not separate mandates.
